content.text: {"headline":"Approve P0 – no action needed; service level is forecast at 97.8% for 16:45–18:45 against an 80% target.","why":"The general queue has been below plan at 16:15 and 16:30 (37 and 35 agents vs 45 and 40), but it was over plan earlier in the afternoon, so staffing is swinging both ways rather than falling. Volume is 8.2% below forecast and handle time is close to forecast. With no changes, payments is predicted at 97.8% and general at 97.7% over the disruption window, with abandons around 0.5%. Sickness (4 vs a usual 2.5) doesn't explain the gap and there is no incident or campaign, so this looks like normal fluctuation. No escalation is required.","trade_offs":["None of the alternatives improve the disruption window: all four plans give the same 97.8% service level and 0.5% abandon rate for 16:45–18:45.","P1 (chat deflection 19:00–20:00) and P3 (chat deflection plus callback) lift the rest-of-day service level from 91.3% to 94.2%, but cost ₹324 and move some customers to chat for a period that is already above target.","P2 (callback 19:00–19:30) is free but only nudges rest of day from 91.3% to 91.6%, and it changes the customer experience for little gain.","No plan puts either queue at risk; payments and general stay at 97.8% and 97.7% under every option."],"watch":"Keep watching agents on the phones for the general queue over the next few intervals. If it keeps falling below plan rather than swinging back, re-run the options. P2 is a free fallback, and P1 is the option to consider if rest-of-day service needs a lift."}
